claim: In the matching retail DLL, FormAnimator.StartOpponentAnm (MethodDef 0x06004E76) selects a Player object by passing its first Int32 argument to PlayerMan.GetPlObj, then dispatches exactly one request call on that Player's animator according to the raw FormAnimator.AnmReqType field: value 2 -> ReqSerialAnm, value 3 -> ReqSkillAnm, value 0 -> ReqBasicAnm, otherwise -> ReqSlotAnm. In verified R6 raw capture bytes, all 847 observed StartOpponentAnm invocations contain exactly one nested request; the first recorded argument, the parent row's recorded target, and the nested request owner_slot are equal in 847/847 cases. The observed branches were 585 ReqBasicAnm and 262 ReqSlotAnm; in all 262 ReqSlotAnm cases the child ResolvedSkillID equals the parent ResolvedSkillID.

evidence.locator: FormAnimator TypeDef RID 2517; StartOpponentAnm MethodDef token 0x06004E76, RVA 0x002DABA8, code size 905, code sha256=4b390293560fe3a02b12845d80419fe4d8747c637a3c94221cf2dac051ffb2cb; dispatch call sites IL+0x3B/0x5D/0x80/0x99 to MethodDef tokens 0x06004E6D/0x06004E6E/0x06004E6F/0x06004E70

847 PRE/POST parent calls; exactly one nested request per parent; 585 ReqBasicAnm, 262 ReqSlotAnm; first recorded arg == parent target == child owner_slot in 847/847; parent/child ResolvedSkillID equal in 262/262 observed ReqSlotAnm branches.

limits: CLR method, field, and parameter names are used only as exact metadata identifiers, not as independent proof of gameplay meaning.
R6 did not exercise the ReqSerialAnm or ReqSkillAnm branches inside StartOpponentAnm; their existence is DLL-proven only in this fact.
This fact closes request selection and host/recipient ownership at the StartOpponentAnm boundary. It does not close packed choreography, damage, animation-bank semantics, or aftermath.
